messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected - serving-runtime errors spike in eu-west (cuda OOMs + container restarts). 5xx rate on /v1/generate jumped to 18% at 05:14Z. Paging on-call.
eli.nguyen: oncall here, looking. Can someone dump earliest pod logs?
maya.p: I'm pulling logs now, seeing repeated OOMs in the large-model workers. snippet: ```
2026-03-14T05:13:56Z serving[worker-42]: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.0 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total, 34.20 GiB already allocated)
Traceback (most recent call last): ...
RestartCount: 7
```
chris_k: Node scale events look... wild. CA bumped node pool eu-west-gpu from 8 -> 26 between 05:10-05:16, then scale-in back to 9 by 05:22. Rapid churn. Looks like scale oscillation induced repeated pod scheduling on noisy hosts.
sara_support: Support flagged 8 paying customers hitting increased latency / 5xxs on high-concurrency endpoints. CSMs notified.
eli.nguyen: hypothesis: autoscaler reacted to CPU/memory pressure but new nodes started containers that immediately OOM due to hotspot batch sizes / cache warmups -> crashloop -> CA sees demand and spins more nodes -> feedback loop. Need to break the loop.
maya.p: I'm going to cordon the most-restarted nodes and drain non-critical workloads. Command I ran: ```kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu | sort -k6``` then ```kubectl cordon ip-10-2-45-19.eu-west```. Drain in progress for node ip-10-2-45-19: ```kubectl drain ip-10-2-45-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```.
ops-bot: automated runbook suggests disabling autoscaler scale-up for target pool for 10m in emergencies. Recommend we patch CA config to increase stabilizationWindowSeconds and set maxNodeProvisionTime.
chris_k: Proposing immediate mitigations: 1) Pause cluster autoscaler for gpu pool (annotation on CA deployment). 2) Reduce serving batch sizes for large-model rollout (env var SERVE_MAX_BATCH=8 -> 4). 3) Route heavy customers to the smaller quantized model variant as fallback.
eli.nguyen: Doing (1) now — kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"cluster-autoscaler","env":[{"name":"SCALE_UP_ENABLED","value":"false"}]}]}}}}' . Will monitor.
maya.p: Reduced batch size via rollout: kubectl set env deploy/serve-large-model SERVE_MAX_BATCH=4 --namespace=redwood-serving ; starting canary 10% -> 100% since immediate risk.
sara_support: Notifying impacted customers: short note going out: "We're seeing elevated errors on high-concurrency generation endpoints caused by node-level GPU OOMs; mitigation underway. We'll post updates every 15m."
eli.nguyen: Traffic switch to fallback variant applied: route rule updated to send requests over concurrency threshold to model:rw-sm-quantized-1. Config change: ```redwood route update --route /v1/generate --fallback-model rw-sm-quantized-1 --threshold 300```
maya.p: Observing pod restart counts dropping after batch size change and cordon. OOM lines are much less frequent. CA CPU/Pod pending counts stabilizing.
chris_k: Logs from previously flapping pod (serve-large-model-7f6d): ```E 05:12:21 CUDA OOM: failed to alloc 1.9GB on /dev/nvidia0; freeing KV cache; restart in 1s``` restarts: 12 -> 2 after mitigations.
ops-bot: Metric snapshot: peak node count 26 at 05:16, sustained node count back to 11 at 05:36. 5xx reduced to 1.2% at 05:30.
eli.nguyen: Confirming impact window ~05:10Z - 05:30Z (roughly 20m). Customer-facing timeline + root cause to be drafted.
sara_support: Logged incident tickets for the 8 affected customers and started one-off log bundles for compliance.
maya.p: Remaining tasks: - re-enable autoscaler with tuning; - audit serving memory usage per variant; - add protective mem limits for worker containers.
chris_k: Action: increase CA stabilization window to 6m and set maxNodes to 20 for gpu pool; also set scaleDownDelay to 10m to avoid immediate contractions. Will create PR against infra repo.
eli.nguyen: Handoff to next oncall Maya at 06:00Z. I'll keep watch for 30m then hand off. :thumbsup:
sara_support: Draft for customers: "Mitigation: we temporarily routed traffic to a smaller model and reduced batch sizes while we stabilized nodes. Impact: increased latency and errors for some high-concurrency requests between 05:10-05:30Z; customers on default routes now back to normal. Follow-up: we will throttle autoscaler oscillation and add memory guards to prevent reoccurrence."
ops-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
eli.nguyen: Closing pager. Post-incident actions: 1) Postmortem (owner: chris_k) 2) Infra PR to tweak CA config (owner: chris_k) 3) Serve change to enforce per-model memory headroom (owner: maya.p) 4) Support follow-ups + customer comms (owner: sara_support).
maya.p: Thanks all. I'll start the infra PR and schedule a deep-dive on memory/KV cache behavior next week.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 05:36Z.
